en: Taal Volcano contains a small island inside a crater lake, which sits inside another island inside a massive lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is so massive that it has its own complete weather system inside the dark cave.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle possesses the longest wings of any eagle, allowing it to glide effortlessly through dense forests.
The famous Chocolate Hills of Bohol consist of over a thousand perfectly symmetrical, cone-shaped limestone formations that turn brown in summer.
The Sibuyan Sea is nicknamed the Galapagos of Asia because it hosts very rare and unique marine wildlife found nowhere else.
Mount Pulag is famous for its thick sea of clouds, which forms when cold mountain air meets warmer valley air.
The tiny Philippine tarsier found in Bohol has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
Lake Taal is the lowest elevation lake in the Philippines, sitting completely below sea level inside a volcanic caldera.
If you lined up the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces end to end, they would stretch halfway around the entire globe.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over four hundred kilometers like a narrow bridge toward Borneo.
Mount Mayon in Albay is widely known for having the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone shape in the entire world.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash and gas that it temporarily cooled the entire planet.
